question.text: A close-ended Cat III AIF (e.g., Vindhya Event-Driven Fund launched for 5 years with a 2-year lock-in) has which of the following redemption characteristics?

answer.text: Investors can redeem freely at daily NAV from day one
Investors cannot redeem during the lock-in; after the lock-in, redemptions may be permitted with an exit load as specified in the PPM, until the fund tenure expires
Investors can redeem only if SEBI issues a specific approval for each exit
Investors are entitled to unrestricted quarterly redemption at any time

explanation.text: **The Logic:** Close-ended AIFs typically have a lock-in (often 1-2 years) after which redemptions are allowed subject to an Exit Load specified in the PPM. Unrestricted redemption is not available; the fund is designed to hold capital through the tenure. **The Trap:** Option A describes open-ended Cat III. Option C is fabricated. Option D overstates investor flexibility for close-ended. **Cross-Exam Context:** Cat I/II is close-ended only (XIX-A/D territory). For Cat III, close-ended is one of two choices. **Manager's Pro-Tip:** When you design a close-ended Cat III scheme, set the exit-load schedule to taper (say, 3% in Y2-3, 2% in Y3-4, 1% in Y4-5) — this protects remaining investors from forced-selling impact from early exits.
